explanation: The pole fires on the last token of a finite clause's subject when that subject is third-person singular: a singular count noun or name ('the colleague', 'Casca', 'the watch', 'Logic'), a 3sg pronoun ('It', 'it', 'he', 'everyone'), or a relative pronoun with a singular antecedent ('that', 'which') — exactly the slot where the clause's finite verb must take the -s agreement form; it stays high through an adverb in the subject-adverb slot ('also', 'quickly', 'often') and drops to zero at the finite verb or auxiliary itself (' is', ' has', ' will', ' left'). It is quiet on plural, first- and second-person subjects ('they', 'we', 'I', 'you', 'the colleagues', 'mice'), at the slot before plural agreement forms (' are', 'were', 'have', 'do'), on the same words in object or predicate-internal position ('it', 'Casca', 'Cassius' as objects), and on complementizer or demonstrative 'that'.
